title: Heren Godot MCP — Fast, powerful, simple. (+Benchmarks!)
author: Lordddddddy
selftext:
There are already a few great MCP servers that connect AI assistants to the Godot engine. Heren takes a different path: instead of starting a fresh Godot process for every request, it keeps a lightweight WebSocket daemon running in the background. Once launched, the engine stays alive and responsive, so the AI can interact with your project almost instantly!

This seemingly small shift makes a HUGE difference in practice:

· Operations complete in around 20ms rather than waiting for a full engine cold start.

· Because Godot remains alive, sub‑resources like collision shapes, materials, and environments are fully persisted in your scene files – something that’s tricky to get right with ephemeral processes.

· Signal connections, batch operations, and script editing all feel smooth and consistent, without the “stop‑and‑go” rhythm of launching and quitting the engine repeatedly.

· A built‑in debug system gives the AI access to breakpoints, stack traces, watch variables, and console output, so it can help you troubleshoot in real time.

· GPU‑accelerated screenshots let the AI literally see the viewport and real-time coordinates, which is incredibly handy for visual feedback.

· The daemon shuts itself down automatically after three minutes of inactivity, so it’s gentle on resources.

All of this is built through 15 carefully designed tools that cover scene management, nodes, resources, scripts, shaders, animations, validation, and debugging.

The project is open source, completely free, and bilingual (English/Spanish).

They said "here be dragons", because they were afraid of their power! 🐉

replies.body: Make sure to issue any problems you have cuz this is very new

comments.author: Eveenah
comments.body: Could you please highlight benefits over simply modifying source files by AI?

replies.author: Lordddddddy
replies.body:
1.- Little to no hallucinations, literally a single syntaxis error will FUCK your scene and corrupt it, which can also lead to destroying the .tscn as a whole sometimes. This is specially tricky with stuff like resources, in fact, the MCP is already tricky because Godot has a VERY specific formatting and serialization, I keep fixing errors almost daily

2.- Less tokens, if you were to modify the files directly, the agent needs to read the file many times, sometimes it is as long as hundreds if not thousands of text, so this would be a RIP for your model. 

3.- More precision, the agent has full control, is able to touch resources to the finest details without hallucinations, though I'm still fixing tons of bugs because of this, but in the end it should be perfect, I know this because my past MCP which was way less efficient fixed this issue. 

  
4.- The MCP, and this is unique to addon/daemon-based MCPs, allows the agent to check coordinates of nodes to "see" the scene + It can run scenes and read the debug, which means it automatically will be able to fix any parsing errors because of hallucinations in .gdscript.

  
5.- This MCP also includes validation tools based on Godot's native CLI, perfect to remove hallucinations even further.
